children: Gold and silver futures fell sharply on Thursday as hotter U.S. wholesale inflation data, surging crude oil prices due to escalating hostilities in the Middle East, and a jump in U.S. Treasury yields raised expectations of a rate increase next week from the Federal Reserve.

The Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.4% last month after an upwardly revised 0.1% gain ​in July, and the PPI advanced 5.4% in the 12 months through August after rising 4.8% in July, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics reported.
Energy prices jumped 4.2% and diesel prices surged 24.1% over the month, and further increases are likely with benchmark Brent crude oil hitting $105/bbl on Thursday.

"This report points to cost increases in the pipeline and will support the case of those on the [Federal Open Market] Committee who want to hike rates now," High Frequency Economics chief economist Carl Weinberg said in a note.
Traders are now pricing in a ​70% chance of an increase in U.S. interest rates next week, up from ​62% before the data, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

title: Gold and silver prices slide as hot producer price data adds to rate-hike bets
